shared_text:
The flight. A twin-engine airliner on an airline flight, climbing after departure from an airport.

The crew. One pilot was the pilot flying and the other the pilot monitoring.

What happened. The crew's clearance, as filed, included a published departure procedure. Before the aircraft entered the runway, the tower amended this to fly runway heading with an initial climb to 2,000 ft, and the crew complied. After take-off they were told to turn to heading 360 and climb, and were handed to the departure controller. Climbing through about 7,000 ft on that heading, they were cleared to 10,000 ft and direct to a fix. Both pilots heard the name of a different fix with a similar-sounding name, which was on their flight plan and on the departure procedure in their original clearance, and the crew read that name back. The readback was not corrected. With the autopilot engaged, the aircraft turned towards the fix the crew had heard and continued climbing towards 10,000 ft.
safe_outcome: While the aircraft was climbing towards 10,000 ft, the crew received a TCAS resolution advisory to monitor vertical speed. The pilot flying disconnected the autopilot and followed it, and the aircraft reached about 10,300 ft. Neither pilot saw the other aircraft. At about the same time the departure controller asked whether they were going direct to the assigned fix; when the crew named the other fix, the controller repeated the correct one and handed them to the next controller. The crew turned towards the correct fix, reported the advisory to the next controller, and returned to 10,000 ft once clear of conflict. No one was hurt and no aircraft was damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was crossing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.
bracket_fill: [climbing / descending / crossing] = crossing; [this aircraft] = this aircraft
notes: Removed under rule 3: both 'Cause' sections (fix names too alike, CPDLC would help) and 'the error was not trapped' as a characterisation; its factual content is kept as 'The readback was not corrected'. Moved to the safe ending (rule 5, deviation D4): the TCAS resolution advisory, the autopilot disconnect and the response to it, the 10,300 ft peak, not seeing the other aircraft, the controller's query and correction, and the report to the next controller. The narratives give the advisory and the controller's query in different orders ('around the same time' in one; query first in the other), so the shared text stops before both, as the aircraft headed for the wrong fix. Removed under rule 6: the airports, the fix and departure names, the runway and the centre names. Judgement calls: the report gives no aircraft type ('commercial fixed wing'), so 'twin-engine airliner' was used; it gives roles only as pilot flying and pilot not flying, with no captain or first officer, so neither is named; no weather or light is given, so neither is stated. The two narratives differ on when the climb to 10,000 ft was given; narrative 2's version (with the direct-to clearance, at about 7,000 ft) was used. 'Similar-sounding' is how both reporters and the synopsis describe the two names. Bracket 'crossing' because the deviation was lateral, towards a fix other than the one assigned.
